transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Torres (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Redwood CSM), Mark Reynolds (Aurora Head of ML), Priya Nair (Aurora Platform), Diego Lopez (Aurora VP Ops)

Summary: quick renewal/expansion checkin to cover capacity needs, regions, and contract length.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll do a quick health check, capacity ask, regional expansion, then pricing and next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Mark: Yeah that works. thanks Samir. we've been generally happy, latency's been solid, but with the new trading feature our peaks are double what we projected so want to talk reserved capacity.
[00:35] Lena: cool, can you remind me of the current traffic shapes? like peak qps and typical seq lengths?
[00:45] Priya: Sure. right now baseline is about 400 qps, peaks hitting 1.2k for 3-5 minute windows, model sequences around 512 tokens avg, but some longer assistants go to ~1k.
[01:02] Lena: ok that matches what we saw in the telemetry. switching to 2x reserved capacity during market open windows makes sense, we should also think about burst capacity for unexpected spikes.
[01:18] Diego: curious about the cost delta—if we double reserved what does that look like month-over-month versus staying hosted with burst?
[01:30] Samir: Good question. i'll do a side-by-side: reserved capacity commit for 2x gives lower per-token unit cost and guaranteed throughput, hosted with bursts keeps flexibility but you pay the premium for on-demand. i'll include exact comparison in the SOW.
[01:45] Mark: Also can we add eu-west and ap-southeast? compliance wants near-region processing for some european customers.
[01:55] Lena: technically straightforward; we have pre-baked regions but need to test network egress and RTT for your infra. we'll run a 4-region latency matrix and share the results.
[02:12] Priya: for ap-southeast we have a partner cloud region but need to confirm VPC peering options. any gotchas?
[02:22] Lena: just typical routing and NAT config. if you want private deployment in that region, that's a slightly different path (Redwood Private) but for now Hosted + Dedicated pools in region should be fine.
[02:35] Diego: on the security front legal asked about KMS integration and audit logs, and whether Redwood stores any raw messages or if we can disable retention.
[02:48] Samir: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and we expose audit logs; retention policies are configurable. i will attach the SOC 2 and security whitepaper, but Lena can show logs and KMS flow in the bench pack.
[03:05] Lena: quick note—when we ran your POC we saw good KV cache hit rates, that was helping latency. if you bump capacity we should re-tune cache TTLs so cost doesn't spike.
[03:18] Mark: fair. also one ask—can we stretch the SLA to higher 99th percentile for trading hours? our ops needs stricter guarantees during market open.
[03:30] Samir: For dedicated reserved pools we can negotiate higher SLAs tied to a commit; i'll include options for enhanced SLA in the SOW and show the delta.
[03:42] Priya: and contract length—would a 12 month extension with capacity commit be preferable cost-wise? we prefer predictable costs.
[03:52] Samir: yes, 12-month commit typically reduces unit pricing significantly versus month-to-month. i'll model both 6 and 12 month options.
[04:05] Diego: any migration work required to add regions? or is it just routing?
[04:12] Lena: mostly routing and model variant pinning. we'll test model variant compatibility; if you use quantized variants in some regions latency differs slightly. we'll flag any evaluation regressions.
[04:26] Mark: On the competitor side, we've talked to Anthropic and also evaluated self-hosting; Anthropic had lower latency in a eu region test but cost was higher. openai was mentioned for a backup for burst, but we'd rather keep a single vendor if possible.
[04:44] Samir: noted. we'll include fallback policies for bursts and a routing plan that favors your Dedicated capacity first.
[04:55] Alex: quick CRM note—renewal date is 2026-04-30, so we have some runway but want to lock in pricing early. i'll update the record.
[05:06] Mark: good. next steps?
[05:10] Samir: i'll send an updated SOW with pricing for 2x reserved capacity, 12-month and 6-month options, and SLA tiers, target by 2026-03-09.
[05:20] Lena: i'll run the region benchmarks and 99th percentile traces and share by 2026-03-08; i'll also include KV cache tuning recommendations.
[05:30] Priya: i'll send you our VPC diagram and peering contacts by 2026-03-10 so you can scope network work.
[05:38] Diego: legal will want the SOC 2 report and KMS integration docs—who should i send that to?
[05:44] Samir: send to samir@redwood.example and cc alex@redwood.example; i'll make sure legal gets the security pack.
[05:52] Mark: any blockers we should call out?
[05:56] Lena: just the usual—need to validate latency in the new regions and ensure kv cache tuning prevents cost spikes.
[06:04] Samir: sounds good. we'll reconvene after benchmarks and SOW. thanks all.

End of transcript. Some auto-transcription errors present (product name sometimes "Redwood Dedicate" in transcript, minor name swaps).
